cur:catacombs2-marseille-saint-victor-co.summary: Under seven arches, Christ stands at the centre on a mountain from which four rivers flow, crowned by the hand of God, between Peter carrying a cross and Paul; five apostles stand on each side. On the lid two deer drink between trees, an image of Paradise, while two angels hold a panel beneath a Christogram between dolphins; at the right appear the miracle at Cana and the spies carrying the grape cluster from the Promised Land.
facts: The four rivers of Paradise flowing from Christ's mountain recall the rivers of Eden in Genesis 2:10–14, a common Early Christian image of salvation.
The pairing of Cana with the grape cluster of the Promised Land on the lid juxtaposes a New Testament miracle with its Old Testament foreshadowing.
cur:catacombs2-marseille-saint-victor-co.original_title: Sarcophage des compagnes de sainte Ursule

cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-psalm-91-christ.summary: In the heavens the cross-nimbed Christ-Logos, holding a book and seated with angels, is flanked by two women carrying disks with the sun and moon — Mercy shown 'in the morning' and Truth 'every night'. Below, musicians praise him with instruments of ten strings before a walled city, and the righteous flourish like palm trees. It is a psalm 'for the sabbath day'.
facts: The Utrecht Psalter illustrates every psalm and canticle with a lively pen drawing — 166 in all — that translates the words of the text, often literally, into images; in these the Lord of the psalms is regularly shown as the youthful Christ-Logos.
Its text is written in rustic capitals, an archaic script that once led scholars to date the manuscript to the 6th century; the drawings are now recognised as Carolingian.
cur:manuscripts2-utrecht-psalm-91-christ.notes: The figure of the Lord is identified as Christ (the Christ-Logos) following the commentary of the Utrecht University Library's annotated edition, which describes the psalter's consistent practice of drawing the God of the psalms as the youthful Christ. The image is a crop of the drawing from the library's IIIF image server.

cur:manuscripts2-otto-iii-baptism-tempta.summary: At the upper left John baptises Christ, who stands naked in the river while the dove descends from a many-coloured arc of heaven and angels hold his garments; at the upper right Christ turns to the devil, a dark winged figure. In the lower register the devil sets Christ on the pinnacle of the Temple and tempts him again, and Christ, standing with two angels on a hill, sends him away.
facts: The Gospels of Otto III has 276 leaves, twelve canon tables, a double-page portrait of the emperor, four evangelist portraits and 29 full-page miniatures of New Testament scenes; it was produced at Reichenau around 1000.
Its original cover still holds a 10th-century Byzantine ivory of the Dormition of the Virgin.
